title: Death Toll From Myla Ammunition Depot Strike Rises to 38, Mayor Among Dead
detail: The confirmed death toll from the August 28 Russian drone strike on an ammunition depot in Myla (Bucha district, Kyiv Oblast) rose to 38 by August 30, with 20 injured and 4 people still missing as emergency crews continued clearing the site and bomb-disposal teams worked through unexploded munitions. Among the dead was Taras Didych, mayor of the nearby village of Dmytrivka. Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko's government came under renewed criticism after officials confirmed this was the second Ukrainian munitions-storage site near a residential area to be hit within six weeks, prompting Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office to widen its criminal negligence investigation into why explosives were stored beside a care home and residential streets.

title: Russia's Defense Ministry Threatens 'Massive Strikes' on Ukraine's Energy Grid
detail: Russia's Defense Ministry announced on August 30 that it is preparing 'massive strikes' against Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter, framing the threat as retaliation for Ukraine's escalating drone campaign against Russian oil refineries and logistics hubs — which Moscow characterized as attacks on 'civilian infrastructure.' The warning came as Ukrainian forces struck Russia's Kirishi refinery, the country's second-largest, processing roughly 20 million tonnes of crude annually, and followed a month in which Ukraine hit Russian refineries at least 21 times, a monthly record. Overnight into August 30, Russia launched 130 attack drones and 2 Iskander-M ballistic missiles at Ukraine, the third consecutive night of sustained bombardment.

media.caption: Russia's Defense Ministry says it is preparing large-scale strikes on Ukraine's energy grid, August 30, 2026
